policy: US source stages are manifest-defined. Country/source content may declare primary artifacts, columns, sentinel handling, derivations, imputation recipes, and outputs here; executable Python belongs only in shared Populace runtimes.

stages.notes: PUF detail is a primary-source donor and must stay separate from benchmark comparisons. IRS disclosure aggregate rows are replaced from raw PUF aggregate totals before uprating; Forbes top-tail synthesis is not enabled.

stages.survey: IRS SOI Sales of Capital Assets (TY2015) + Pub 1304 Table 1.4

artifacts.locator: SOI Sales of Capital Assets Table 1 (1A/1C), capital gain distributions line
SOI Pub 1304 Table 1.4, capital gain distributions reported on Form 1040

stages.notes: Splits the Schedule D line 13 route of capital gain distributions out of long-term gains as a memo component. No by-AGI CGD series exists in published SOI data (SOCA Table 2 merges CGD into 'Other asset types'), so the v1 split applies the national Schedule-D share of LT net gains proportionally within eligible records; the two reporting routes are mutually exclusive on a real return, so records with direct-route distributions are excluded. Anchor arithmetic, the by-AGI tables that do exist, and follow-ups live in soca_capital_gain_distribution_shares.json.

artifacts.locator: Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances public extract

stages.notes: Sentinel replacement is declared here so impossible negative auto-loan interest is rejected at the source boundary and again at export gates.

artifacts.locator: Census SIPP 2023 public-use slim tip extract; immutable mirror revision 21280dca5995e978d706740a8a4b9b7860cfd7b6

stages.notes: Tip income is the weighted-QRF port pinned to the retired implementation at 9a823603e6b5fb916d65ec45d74c9c7eb0043db1: December SIPP monthly tips across jobs 1-7 times 12, conditioned on employment income, age, child counts, and Treasury tipped occupation. treasury_tipped_occupation_code is mapped directly from CPS ASEC PEIOOCC using the IRS/Treasury 2025-42 tipped-occupation list and Census 2018 occupation/SOC crosswalk. The final retired downloader moved to an unpinned SIPP 2024 zip; this stage deliberately uses the same implementation's sha-pinned 2023 donor that built the reference eCPS.

artifacts.locator: EPI CPS ORG 2024 immutable mirror revision 35054105a3d6797af2e443d3efa9f1d57713ba78

stages.notes: Port of the retired implementation at 9a823603e6b5fb916d65ec45d74c9c7eb0043db1 (datasets/org/org.py and datasets/cps/cps.py). The immutable EPI mirror supplies sha-pinned 2024 CPS ORG donor rows; the final retired predictors, QRF targets, BLS 2024 union-representation assignment, POCCU2 mappings, domain constraints, and FLSA premium-share formula are retained. The final downloader rebuilt the donor from 12 live Census monthly files without content hashes, so this stage pins the retired artifact repository's immutable mirror instead of accepting mutable monthly bytes. Usual weekly hours remain owned by hours_worked (ASEC HRSWK) and are consumed here as the final retired QRF predictor.

artifacts.locator: MEPS Insurance Component plan-type premium tables
Census CPS ASEC person file
Census CPS ASEC person file citizenship (PRCITSHP), entry year (PEINUSYR), nativity (PENATVTY), and program-participation fields
Pew Research Center unauthorized-immigrant population and worker estimates; Higher Ed Immigration Portal undocumented-student estimates

stages.notes: Citizenship is measured (PRCITSHP), not imputed. Non-citizens with any ASEC-UA legal-status indicator (Van Hook et al., SSRN 4662801) become OTHER_NON_CITIZEN. The CPS carries no work-authorization variable, so among residual non-citizens, workers and students spill to NON_CITIZEN_VALID_EAD in deterministic seeded order until the remaining undocumented worker count matches Pew's 8.3M and the undocumented student count matches the Higher Ed Immigration Portal's ~408k — the only forced margins. The total undocumented population is emergent (≈13M on the 2024 ASEC, within the range of published 2023-24 estimates) and is gated against Pew's 11.0M 2022 anchor with a coarse plausibility band rather than forced; reconciling the level is the calibration lane's job. Immigration-status tags carry only statutory tests the data supports: DACA (arrival cohort among EAD holders) and CUBAN_HAITIAN_ENTRANT (nativity plus post-1980 arrival); other documented non-citizens stay LEGAL_PERMANENT_RESIDENT, the modal true status — blanket REFUGEE/TPS labels are deliberately not fabricated because they would mislabel millions and over-grant refugee-class benefit exemptions.

artifacts.locator: Census CPS ASEC person file usual weekly hours (HRSWK), reference-week hours (A_HRS1), and weeks worked (WKSWORK)

stages.notes: Direct mappings of measured ASEC hours variables, identical to the retired enhanced-CPS pipeline: weekly_hours_worked_before_lsr <- HRSWK (usual hours per week last year, 0 for non-workers), hours_worked_last_week <- A_HRS1, weeks_worked <- WKSWORK clipped to [0, 52]. Nothing is imputed. Without this stage PolicyEngine-US defaults every person to 40 weekly hours, so the SNAP 30-hour general and 20-hour ABAWD work requirements pass universally (populace #242/#248). HRSWK is an annual usual-hours measure while the ABAWD standard is a monthly 80-hour test; week-by-week volatility is not observable in the CPS and is deliberately out of scope.

stages.survey: Census CPS ASEC + USDA FNS participation rate estimates

artifacts.locator: Census CPS ASEC SPM unit reported SNAP subsidy (SPM_SNAPSUB)
USDA FNS SNAP participation-rate estimates (Reaching Those in Need)

stages.notes: Reported recipients (SPM_SNAPSUB > 0) always take up — survey measurement first. Non-reporting units receive seeded draws at exactly the rate needed for the overall weighted take-up share to land on the cited FNS participation rate; when reporters alone exceed the rate the share is emergent. The flag is assigned across all SPM units and the engine intersects it with modeled eligibility, matching the retired enhanced-CPS pipeline. Draws are keyed by stable source identity so support-channel clones of one source unit always agree. Without this stage the engine defaults every unit to take-up (100% participation), overstating the reach of eligibility-side reforms (populace #243).

artifacts.locator: Census CPS ASEC person file disability-difficulty items (PEDISDRS/PEDISEAR/PEDISEYE/PEDISOUT/PEDISPHY/PEDISREM), school enrollment (A_HSCOL, A_FTPT), parent line pointers (PEPAR1, PEPAR2), veterans' payments (VET_VAL), and reported SSI (SSI_VAL)

stages.notes: Direct mappings of measured ASEC demographic variables reproducing the retired enhanced-CPS pipeline's constructions (each cited to the retired pipeline's source files in the stage module): is_disabled <- any PEDIS* difficulty item == 1, aligned with reported SSI (under-65 SSI_VAL > 0 implies disabled — the retired align_reported_ssi_disability rule from datasets/cps/takeup.py, applied to is_disabled in cps.py); is_blind <- PEDISEYE == 1; is_full_time_college_student <- A_HSCOL == 2 & A_FTPT == 1 (the retired primary branch; census_cps.py loads A_FTPT, so the published surface ran the strict form — the A_HSCOL-only fallback for loads without A_FTPT is not reproduced); own_children_in_household <- count of household members whose PEPAR1/PEPAR2 parent pointers resolve to the person within PH_SEQ; veterans_benefits <- VET_VAL. Nothing is imputed. Without this stage every input takes its engine default (False/0), erasing SNAP disability, student, parent/child, and veteran exemption channels (populace #244/#248). is_veteran is formula-owned in PolicyEngine-US (derived from veterans_benefits) and is deliberately not exported (populace #24).

stages.survey: Census CPS ASEC + CDC natality-derived national pregnancy rate

artifacts.locator: Census CPS ASEC person file sex (A_SEX) and age (A_AGE)
CDC NCHS natality-derived point-in-time pregnancy rate among women 15-44 (births x 39/52 over female 15-44 population)

stages.notes: The CPS ASEC does not ask about pregnancy, so is_pregnant is seeded rather than mapped, matching the retired enhanced-CPS pipeline: women aged 15-44 receive stable blake2b draws against the pregnancy rate (point-in-time rate = annual births x 39/52 over the female 15-44 population; 4.1% nationally, the retired pipeline's national rate). The retired pipeline varied the rate by state using live CDC VSRR + Census ACS fetches; populace builds are hermetic, so the national rate applies uniformly and state-level variation is follow-up work under populace #351. Without this stage is_pregnant defaults to False for everyone and the SNAP ABAWD pregnancy exemption (7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(3)(E)) never fires.

stages.survey: Census CPS ASEC + statutory exemption cap (7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(6))

artifacts.locator: Census CPS ASEC person file age (A_AGE)
Statutory ABAWD discretionary exemption cap: 8% of covered individuals from FY2024 (7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(6); 15% FY1998-2019, 12% FY2020-23)

stages.notes: State agencies may exempt a monthly-average share of ABAWD-covered individuals from the SNAP time limit (7 U.S.C. 2015(o)(6)): 8% from FY2024 (15% FY1998-2019, 12% FY2020-23) — the cap PolicyEngine-US carries as gov.usda.snap.work_requirements.abawd.discretionary_exemption_rate. Coverage is engine logic the build must not duplicate, so the flag is seeded with stable blake2b draws across the potentially covered population (adults 18-64) and the engine intersects it with modeled coverage; draws being independent of coverage keeps the exempt share among covered individuals at the statutory rate in expectation. Seeding at the cap assumes full state usage, which overstates actual practice: USDA reporting shows states typically use well under the allotment (exemption usage exceeded the cap in only five state-year instances across FY2016-19), so this is an upper bound on the discretionary channel; refining toward USDA exemption-usage reports is follow-up under populace #323. Without this stage the input defaults to False and the discretionary channel never fires (populace #323).
The conversion is a declarative structural transform over PUF and SCF outputs, not a benchmark data loader.

stages.survey: CPS ASEC reported coverage + CMS Medicaid monthly enrollment snapshot

artifacts.locator: CPS ASEC current Medicaid coverage at interview (has_medicaid_health_coverage_at_interview)
CMS Medicaid and CHIP monthly enrollment, December 2024 state snapshot (cms_medicaid.month2024_12.state_enrollment.*.total_medicaid_enrollment)

stages.notes: Anchored count-calibration (take-up contract treatment: count_calibrated; populace #331). Eligible reporters always take up; the fill draws at an in-build state rate (CMS count over weighted modeled eligibles, an assignment prior, never cited as provenance) and is greedily calibrated to the CMS December 2024 state snapshot among eligible non-anchored persons. Point-in-time (average-month) enrollment semantics per #332 - never ever-enrolled-in-year counts. The assign operation deliberately carries no eligibility mask: off-domain persons keep a draw-based propensity so eligibility-expanding reforms do not inherit a hard-coded zero response; the engine's is_medicaid_eligible gate hides the flag at baseline. States whose CMS count meets or exceeds modeled eligible weight saturate (all eligibles enroll) and are recorded as saturated in diagnostics, not failed (#170's eligibility-undercount shortfall is out of scope). CHIP deliberately excluded pending the #321 M-CHIP/separate-CHIP ledger concept split.
